doc.title: Arturo Sandoval interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 12, 2023

title: 'Anybody can play ugly': tone and learning from singers
summary: He puts tone quality first and tells students to learn lyrics and listen to singers such as Nat King Cole and Ella Fitzgerald, demonstrating with 'When I Fall in Love'.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: I heard you say a phrase in an interview, “You should play pretty, anybody can play ugly.”

I, you know, because some people they’re not concentrating on certain things. The first thing we must care about is the quality of the tone, the quality of the sound. We must produce a good sound, in tune and warm and pretty and good sound. That’s the number one priority. But also I recommend my students for example, to listen to good singers. And even some old timers are recommended, to learn the lyrics of a song. You understand what I mean? There’s two different ways to play a melody.
Okay I think that qualifies as ugly.
Yes. Absolutely. But if you think about how for example Nat King Cole or Ella Fitzgerald would sing that, you’d rewind and say let me try it again.
You’re singing, you understand what I mean? You’re even making implicit the lyrics even if you’re playing instrumental.
